name: Scorpion
summary: The scorpion answers a speed-up fired straight at your body. You drop into a squat until your paddle hand is below the top of the net, hold the paddle up in front of your face like a scorpion's tail, and punch the ball back out — so a ball that would have jammed your backhand becomes a forehand counter at their feet. Zane Navratil named it for what you look like doing it.
whenToUse: Your dink landed low and short, so their only option is to hit up at you.
The opponent is lined up directly across from you, with no angle available.
The speed-up is coming at your chest or your paddle-side shoulder, where a backhand block cramps.
You read it early enough to get down — the drop has to happen before the ball does.
howTo: Read the speed-up before it leaves their paddle: a low ball at their feet is the tell.
Bend your knees and drop until your paddle hand is below the top of the net tape.
Bring the paddle up and out so it sits in front of your face, wrist firm and still.
Meet the ball in front of you and punch outward, not downward.
Send it back through the middle at the feet of whoever attacked you.
Stand up and get the paddle back to your chest — the reply comes fast.
commonMistakes: Staying tall and calling it a scorpion. Above the tape it is an ordinary block.
Punching down at the ball. From below the net there is no angle down, so it goes into the tape.
Trying it when they have pulled you wide — from down there you cannot cover the line and the middle at once.
Dropping too late, so the ball arrives while you are still on the way down.
Doing it on every speed-up until they simply aim at your feet instead.

drills.name: Below the tape
drills.description: Your partner dinks, then speeds one up at your chest without warning. You may only counter from a squat with your paddle hand below the net tape — anything you hit standing up does not count, however good it was.

drills.name: Punch out, not down
drills.description: Same feed, but a towel is laid over the net tape on your side. Every ball has to come off your paddle flat and outward, over the towel — if you swing down you hit it. It fixes the one mistake that makes this shot fail.

mistake.label: Punched downward from below the net: there is no angle down to be had, so the ball goes into the tape.

rows.label: Body position
rows.self: Squat until your paddle hand is under the net tape.
rows.other: Stay in your normal ready position.

rows.label: Paddle
rows.self: Up and out in front of your face.

rows.label: What comes back
rows.self: A forehand counter down at their feet.
rows.other: A soft ball that dies in their kitchen.

rows.label: Needs
rows.self: An early read and an opponent straight across from you.
rows.other: Nothing but a still paddle — it works from anywhere.
